FXbatch Resizer v2.5.0 User Guide

Batch Image Resizing, Format Conversion, and Compression

User manual and technical documentation for batch image processing, format conversion, and metadata management.

1. Overview and Core Architecture

FXbatch Resizer converts, resizes, and recompresses entire folders of images. The application runs on Python 3.12, CustomTkinter, and Pillow (PIL) with libavif. File conversions run in a background worker thread so the user interface remains responsive throughout batch jobs.

Background Processing

Image processing tasks run on a separate thread and dispatch status updates through a thread-safe queue. The window stays responsive without freezing during large jobs.

Sample Image Telemetry

When you select a folder, FXbatch processes the first image immediately. It calculates converted dimensions, file size estimates, and the percentage reduction before you commit to processing the full batch.

Non-Destructive File Handling

Your source images remain untouched. FXbatch saves converted files either to a dedicated LowRes subfolder or to a separate destination folder of your choice.

2. User Interface and Layout Guide

The interface is arranged into two areas: configuration options on the left sidebar and live preview with batch details on the right.

Left Configuration Sidebar

  • Directory selection: Choose input and output folders with the browse button ... or by dragging a folder directly from Windows File Explorer into the dropzone.
  • Destination mode: Switch between LowRes Subfolder (creates a subfolder inside the input directory) and Custom Folder (saves files to any chosen directory).
  • Output format: Dropdown supporting .JPG, .PNG, .WEBP, .AVIF, and .ICO.
  • Sizing controls: Adapts its input fields to the chosen sizing mode:
    • Percentage (%): Slider and input box to scale images between 5% and 200%.
    • Bounding Box: Maximum width and height constraints that preserve the original aspect ratio.
    • Target Width: Sets a fixed width and calculates the height proportionally.
    • Target Height: Sets a fixed height and calculates the width proportionally.
    • ICO Resolution: Select an icon preset (16 to 256 pixels) or generate a multi-resolution bundle.
  • Compression quality: Slider and text input (10 to 100) for lossy encoders.
  • DPI resolution: Sets metadata print resolution (1 to 3000 DPI).
  • Resampling filter: Options include Lanczos, Bicubic, Bilinear, Box, and Nearest.
  • Reset settings button: Restores all sidebar controls to the saved values from config.ini.

Right Preview and Telemetry Area

  • Sample preview: Renders a scaled preview of the first image in the folder, displaying the filename in the top-right label.
  • Resample preview button: Recalculates the sample image when you change sizing, quality, or format options.
  • Sample analysis card: Compares source and converted dimensions, aspect ratio, file size, and space saved.
  • Batch telemetry: Three counters track ready files, elapsed time, and completion percentage.
  • Progress simulation: A 2.5-second setup animation precedes active file conversion.
  • Log console: Displays a single status line during processing, replaced by a complete summary report once finished.
  • Open output folder: Appears in the bottom status bar after batch completion so you can open the target folder in File Explorer with one click.

3. Supported Formats and Codecs

FXbatch supports five export formats for digital photography, web publishing, user interface graphics, and Windows desktop application icons.

Format File Extension Compression Alpha Channel DPI Metadata Typical Use Case
JPEG .jpg, .jpeg Lossy (DCT) No Yes (JFIF and EXIF) Photos, general archives, and high-compatibility web imagery.
PNG .png Lossless (Deflate) Yes (32-bit RGBA) Yes (pHYs chunk) Screenshots, diagrams, UI elements, and transparent artwork.
WebP .webp Lossy and Lossless Yes Yes (EXIF) Web delivery with smaller file sizes than JPEG.
AVIF .avif Lossy (AV1 Intra) Yes Yes Modern web publishing with high detail retention at low bitrates.
Windows Icon .ico BMP and PNG Container Yes (ARGB) N/A (Fixed pixels) Application icons, desktop shortcuts, and web favicons.

Windows Icon (.ICO) Features

When selecting .ICO format, FXbatch provides dedicated icon generation options:

  • Standard presets: Create single-resolution icons at 16x16, 24x24, 32x32, 48x48, 64x64, 128x128, or 256x256 pixels.
  • Multi-resolution bundle: Select Multi-Resolution Bundle to pack all seven standard resolutions into a single .ico file. Windows then selects the right size based on screen scaling and folder view settings.
  • Aspect ratio check: Windows icons require square (1:1) dimensions. FXbatch checks the source image aspect ratio and displays an alert if it is not 1:1, helping prevent unintended image stretching.

4. Sizing Modes and Resampling Filters

Image dimensions and pixel scaling are governed by five sizing modes and five interpolation filters.

Percentage (%) Scaling

Multiplies width and height by a percentage from 5% to 200%. Values under 100% downscale images; values over 100% upscale them.

Bounding Box (Max W × Max H)

Constrains images inside maximum width and height bounds while keeping original proportions. The first dimension that reaches the limit sets the final scale.

Target Width Mode

Sets a fixed width in pixels (such as 1920px). Height is calculated automatically: h = round(w × orig_h / orig_w).

Target Height Mode

Sets a fixed height in pixels (such as 1080px). Width is calculated automatically: w = round(h × orig_w / orig_h).

Interpolation Filters

Filter Description Sharpness Speed Best Use
Lanczos 3-lobe sinc-windowed filter: sinc(x) × sinc(x/3) High Moderate Downscaling photography; keeps edges and fine text sharp.
Bicubic Cubic spline interpolation with smooth gradients Medium-High Fast Enlargements and photographs with soft color transitions.
Bilinear Linear interpolation across a 2×2 pixel area Medium Very Fast Quick drafts and preview batches.
Box Pixel area averaging Low Fastest Downscaling large batches where speed takes priority over sharpness.
Nearest Nearest-neighbor point sampling without smoothing Hard edge Instant Pixel art, retro game assets, and sharp icon grids.

5. Settings and Naming Tokens

The Settings window configures default startup options, file collision behavior, folder preferences, and output filename templates. You can open it using the gear icon in the header or by pressing Ctrl+S.

Settings Reference

  • FXbatch Version: Shows the active engine release version (such as 2.5.0).
  • Startup Theme: Choose whether the app launches in Dark mode, Light mode, or System (follows your Windows setting).
  • Collision Policy: Determines what happens when an output file already exists in the destination folder:
    • Overwrite (default): Replaces the existing file in the destination.
    • Auto-Rename: Appends a number like photo_1.jpg so no file is overwritten.
    • Skip Existing: Leaves the existing file in place, skips processing it, and notes the skip in the log.
  • Open Destination: Checkbox that opens File Explorer to the output folder when a batch finishes. Default is off.
  • Default Quality: Baseline quality setting for lossy formats (10 to 100, default 60).
  • Default Resize %: Baseline resize percentage (5% to 200%, default 40%).
  • Default DPI: Baseline print resolution in dots per inch (1 to 3000, default 72 for screens, 300 for print).
  • Subfolder Name: Name of the subfolder created in source directories when using subfolder mode (default LowRes).

Naming Template Variables

You can customize output filenames by adding variables to the NAMING TEMPLATE field. Moving your mouse over the field displays helpful tips and examples.

Variable Description Example Value
{name} Original filename without extension. (Required) vacation_photo
{w} Converted output width in pixels. 1920
{h} Converted output height in pixels. 1080
{orig_w} Original source width in pixels. 4032
{orig_h} Original source height in pixels. 3024
{quality} Compression quality value used. 60

Example Filename Templates

Template Source File Output File Common Application
{name} product.png product.jpg Standard 1:1 filename preservation.
{name}_{w}x{h} banner.jpg banner_1920x1080.jpg Responsive web graphics with dimensions in the name.
{name}_lowres catalog.png catalog_lowres.jpg Low-resolution proofs for email attachments.
{name}_thumb portrait.jpg portrait_thumb.webp Thumbnail generation for galleries.
{name}_q{quality} photo.jpg photo_q60.avif Quality test comparisons.

6. Production Workflow

A typical batch workflow follows these steps:

  1. Select input folder: Drag a folder into the dropzone or click ... next to the Input Folder field. FXbatch scans the folder and queues supported image files.
  2. Set destination mode:
    • Select LowRes Subfolder to save output files in a subfolder inside the input directory.
    • Select Custom Folder to save output files in a separate folder you choose.
  3. Choose format and sizing: Pick an output format (such as .JPG or .WEBP) and set your sizing mode (such as Percentage (%) or Bounding Box).
  4. Set quality and filter: Adjust the compression quality slider (default 60) and select a resampling filter like Lanczos for downscaling.
  5. Review sample analysis: Check the Sample Analysis card on the right to review the converted dimensions, aspect ratio check, and file size estimates. Click Resample Preview to refresh the thumbnail.
  6. Run the batch: Click Start Batch Process or press Ctrl+Enter. When processing finishes, click Open Output Folder to view your new files.

7. Collision Safety and File Protections

FXbatch includes safeguards to prevent data loss and keep processing stable during heavy workloads.

Same-Folder Protection

If you set the output destination to the same folder as the input folder and the output format matches the source files without renaming tokens, FXbatch stops and prompts you to choose another folder, preventing accidental overwrites of original files.

Memory Management

Images are read through buffered streams, and file handles close right after conversion. This keeps memory usage steady even when processing thousands of files.

Thread Isolation

All encoding and disk operations run in a background worker thread. Updates pass to the main interface through a queue, keeping the window responsive while files are being processed.

9. Troubleshooting and FAQ

Q: Why is my converted file larger than the original?

This happens when you upscale an image beyond 100%, or when converting a compressed JPEG into a lossless PNG. PNG preserves all raw pixel data without lossy discarding.

Q: Why does the ICO format show an aspect ratio warning?

Windows icons must be square (1:1). If your source image is rectangular, FXbatch warns you so you know the resulting icon might look compressed horizontally or vertically.

Q: Does FXbatch modify my original files?

No. Source images are opened in read-only mode and saved as newly generated files in your chosen destination directory.

Q: Where are my settings saved?

Settings are stored in config.ini. In development, the file sits alongside the script. In installed builds, settings are saved in %APPDATA%\FXbatch\config.ini.

Q: What happens if an image in the batch is corrupted?

FXbatch catches the error, logs the filename in the summary report, and continues processing the rest of the folder without stopping the batch.
